samples.summary: The canonical error-contract section of cli.md (~§ lines 901–924) was left describing the behavior this change replaces, so the doc now carries two competing descriptions of the same contract. Line 902 still says "packages/cli/src/errors.ts holds the whole contract"; the table row at line 911 still promises `command-specific or ERROR` for a 400/404/409, whereas `upstreamErrorCode()` now emits `HTTP_ERROR` for those; and lines 919–922 still describe `throw httpError(status)` plus per-command verbatim printing as the pattern "at every non-OK response", which is exactly what `forwardUpstreamError`/`upstreamErrorJson` replaced. The new prose was appended in §10 rather than folded into the section that already owned this contract — the repo's stated docs discipline is to fold into the canonical write-up, not to add a parallel one.

Failure classification is reinvented in the output layer instead of reused from `errors.ts`. `UpstreamHttpError` re-implements what `SystemError`/`UserError` already provide (a `code` plus an `exitCode` that `outputError` reads), and `upstreamErrorCode(status)` is a second status→code classifier alongside `httpError()` in errors.ts — and the two disagree (httpError yields a plain Error → `ERROR` for a 4xx, upstreamErrorCode yields `HTTP_ERROR`), while the new doc text and the code comment both claim it is the "same classification `httpError()` applies". cli.md's own file map assigns classification to `errors.ts` (line 759) and formatter.ts to "Format dispatcher (json|table|csv|yaml)" (line 812); the map was updated for the new `client/url.ts` but not for ~230 lines of classification/bounding logic landing in formatter.ts.

`assertNoDotSegments` is a second implementation of the rule the change explicitly centralizes ("two copies of a security rule drift", url.ts). It is defense-in-depth for a caller that forgets `seg()`, but it re-encodes the refusal set in a different shape (split-on-'/' vs. exact value check) in the CLI only — the frontend has no equivalent backstop. A shared assertion in `@wafflebase/core/url` next to `seg()` would keep one definition.
searchedFor: grep seg( in packages/cli/src and packages/frontend/src

samples.summary: The dry-run centralization is partial: `runDocsImport`, `runNotesImport` and `runSlidesImport` still hand-roll their own preview payload (`{method, path, body}` via `io.stdout`) instead of going through `printDryRun`, so they get neither the `url` shape the doc calls "the request that would be sent" nor the dot-segment backstop the printer now applies. Same preview concern, two builders — the thing §10 argues against.

The pre-existing matrix row "Download returned 2xx with no bytes … (backend body, else `{ error: { code: \"HTTP_ERROR\" } }`)" now misdescribes `runFilesDownload`, which no longer prints the backend body for that case but a fixed synthesized message (`HTTP <status> carried no file content for document <id>`). The behavior change is real and deliberate (the diff comments on it) but the row it contradicts was not touched.

Scope breadth: the change bundles three independent concerns — one-segment id encoding (core + CLI + entire frontend API layer), unification of the non-OK response envelope (`forwardUpstreamError`/`upstreamErrorJson`, ~30 call sites), and opt-in image-failure tolerance in the shared PDF/DOCX/PPTX exporters — plus an unrelated `files download` fallback-filename change. No originating issue text was supplied with this review, so acceptance criteria could not be checked; as landed, none of the three can be reverted independently.

`seg(String(userId))` applies the path-segment guard to a `number` parameter, where neither traversal nor encoding is possible. Harmless, but it reads as the rule being applied mechanically rather than where an untrusted string enters a path.

Two files whose entire content is `export { seg } from '@wafflebase/core/url'` (CLI + frontend). The stated rationale is layering, but the indirection means a reader of a call site has to hop twice to find the rule, and the docs already point at core as the home.
searchedFor: read packages/cli/src/client/url.ts and packages/frontend/src/api/url.ts diff hunks

verdict.reason: The absence claim ("new prose appended in §10 rather than folded into the section that owns the error contract; no canonical update") has a direct counterexample: §10 "Error Matrix" (docs/design/cli.md:1473) IS the canonical error-contract section, and it was updated in place — the matrix rows at 1491–1492 were rewritten to the new envelope-vs-non-envelope rule with HTTP_ERROR/AUTH_ERROR/SERVER_ERROR by status (matching upstreamErrorCode, packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:258–262), and the prose at 1514–1527 explicitly retires the old per-call-site pattern. It is inside the canonical subsystem doc, not a parallel file. The originating acceptance criteria name that exact location (docs/tasks/active/20260811-cli-upstream-error-envelope-todo.md:82, 103–104: "Documented in packages/cli/README.md and docs/design/cli.md §10" / "docs/design/cli.md's error matrix document HTTP_ERROR"), with the README half at packages/cli/README.md:141–164. The alleged staleness in §8.1 is also weaker than described: errors.ts:55–84 still defines exitCodeForStatus and httpError, and httpError is still thrown at non-OK responses (docs/image-fetcher.ts:863, docs/pdf-export.ts:40), and formatter.ts:251–262 deliberately mirrors httpError's classification "so the error matrix in docs/design/cli.md holds regardless of which path reported the failure", so §8.1's 401/403 → AUTH_ERROR, 5xx → SERVER_ERROR, 4xx → exit 1 rows remain accurate. What remains — row 911 not listing HTTP_ERROR and lines 919–922 saying "verbatim"/per-site phrasing — is a wording-freshness cleanup in a summary paragraph whose precise contract §10 owns: a minor consistency nit, which never blocks under this lens's rubric.

finding.summary: Failure classification is reinvented in the output layer instead of reused from `errors.ts`. `UpstreamHttpError` re-implements what `SystemError`/`UserError` already provide (a `code` plus an `exitCode` that `outputError` reads), and `upstreamErrorCode(status)` is a second status→code classifier alongside `httpError()` in errors.ts — and the two disagree (httpError yields a plain Error → `ERROR` for a 4xx, upstreamErrorCode yields `HTTP_ERROR`), while the new doc text and the code comment both claim it is the "same classification `httpError()` applies". cli.md's own file map assigns classification to `errors.ts` (line 759) and formatter.ts to "Format dispatcher (json|table|csv|yaml)" (line 812); the map was updated for the new `client/url.ts` but not for ~230 lines of classification/bounding logic landing in formatter.ts.

verdict.reason: The code exists roughly where located, but it is not a fit violation under this lens. (a) Placement is spec-mandated: the originating issue says to add the guard in src/output/formatter.ts and to classify via one shared `upstreamErrorCode` shared with `upstreamErrorJson` (todo:21-26, :126-131). (b) The alleged "disagreement" with httpError() is a required acceptance criterion — an Express-shaped 404 body must report HTTP_ERROR/exit 1 (todo:65-72); reusing httpError() (plain Error for 4xx → code ERROR, errors.ts:75-84) would violate it, and cli.md:1492 vs :1506 document the two rows as deliberately distinct. (c) The classification does reuse errors.ts where reuse is possible (exitCodeFor, exitCodeForStatus, AUTH_FAILED_MESSAGE — formatter.ts:5-9,243,284); only a 3-line status→code map is local, i.e. a placement preference = minor, never blocking. (d) The quoted claim is misread: the comment at formatter.ts:250-256 scopes sameness to auth/server and explicitly names the divergence ("Everything else is the plain HTTP_ERROR"), and no doc text claims httpError-identical classification. (e) Design-doc discipline is satisfied: the canonical cli.md was updated for this change (matrix row :1492, guard section :1514-1527, bounding table :1611-1626); only the §7 one-line file map (:812) is stale, which is a nit.

finding.summary: Reviewer did not produce a valid verdict: review: every credential in the pool (2) was retired — nothing left to fail over to

verdict.reason:
The "finding" is not a claim about repository code at all — it is verbatim the operational error string the review harness itself emits when its CI credential pool is exhausted. `poolExhaustedError()` in `scripts/agent/ask.mjs:630-637` builds exactly the message `"<label>: every credential in the pool (<n>) was retired — nothing left to fail over to"` with `kind: "pool-exhausted"`, and the "Reviewer did not produce a valid verdict" prefix is the panel's INFRA path reporting that a lens never returned output. That behaviour is deliberate and covered by unit tests (`scripts/agent/ask.test.mjs:302`, `:321`, `:341`), and the repo already tracks the underlying capacity/failover issue as an infrastructure task, explicitly noting "the page came from the INFRA path, so no gate was ever consulted" (`docs/tasks/active/20260820-fixer-live-credential-todo.md:8-11`, `:31-40`).

Under the design-fit / spec-conformance rubric there is nothing to adjudicate: the finding cites no file or line, no unmet `outcome`/`acceptance` criterion, no duplicated module, no exceeded Non-Goal, and no missing/parallel `docs/design/` doc. It is a review-runner failure (the lens crashed on credential exhaustion before producing a verdict), i.e. out of this lens's lane and not a blocking defect in the change. Judged charitably as a code claim it is also not a defect: the exhaustion throw is the intended single-source-of-truth error for "pool had credentials and all are retired", documented at `scripts/agent/ask.mjs:607-629`.
